Chapter 18
Reporting in SAP S/4HANA
Timely, accurate, and comprehensive information helps companies
make better and faster business decisions. You can immediately start to
use the many information systems, standard reports, standard analyses,
and SAP Fiori apps available in SAP S/4HANA for QM and other logistics
areas.
This chapter provides detailed guidance on how to leverage several standard reports
and SAP Fiori apps that are available in all areas of SAP S/4HANA. We’ll cover standard
reports such as information systems that are available for day-to-day reporting, as well
as many standard analyses and several SAP Fiori apps available to help business pro-
cess owners make important and better decisions. After you become familiar with the
features and functions for reporting, including tools and menu bars, it becomes easier
to navigate to unexplored areas of reporting.
In this chapter, we’ll cover the information systems of QM, including the options to lever-
age several functions beneficial to business users, such as the ability to create various
graphs from the data. After we cover the options for reporting with real-time informa-
tion in the information systems, we’ll discuss how to report on historical data with stan-
dard analyses available for the QM area, as well as some of the associated features, such as
time series and ABC analysis. We’ll also cover the QM cockpit for evaluations, as well as
the several SAP Fiori apps for QM in areas of analytics, master data, and transactions.
Note
For more reports and reporting options, we suggest that you read Chapter 12 on quality
notification and Chapter 19 on quality control.
18.1 The Basics of Reporting
To take full advantage of your SAP S/4HANA system, it’s essential that you become
familiar with the toolbars and other features frequently available for use in reports.
Because these functions are the same in all the information systems and analyses,
you’ll begin to navigate faster and be able to quickly get to your desired information or
even find tips and tricks to manage the display and availability of data as needed.

18 Reporting in SAP S/4HANA
772
In the next sections, you’ll learn how to leverage the standard reports and standard
analyses in QM. Then, we’ll show you how to use the QM Cockpit for Evaluations. After
that, we’ll devote a significant portion of this chapter to covering SAP Fiori apps for QM.
As new SAP Fiori apps are constantly added with each SAP S/4HANA release, we also
cover how to find and explore them and begin taking advantage of the business bene-
fits they offer.
18.1.1 Inspection Lot Selection
When we say inspection lot selection, we’re talking about an information system that
consists of the most up-to-date information about a specific object and is based on the
transactions that the business user has performed as part of the business process. For
example, when you execute the inspection lot selection, the system displays the cur-
rent status of various inspection lots, including those for which results recording or a
usage decision has happened. If you run the same report again after six hours, for
example, when the business user has recorded more results or a usage decision, the
system shows up-to-date (and different) information. This information helps to reflect
the accurate and up-to-date status of various activities and business processes.
We’ve divided the large number of available options for parameters selection into sev-
eral figures in the following sections for ease of understanding and comprehension.
Figure 18.1 Inspection Lot Selection

18.1.2 Multiple Selection
You may have noticed that on the selection screen of a report, an option is available to
enter any parameter in a range or an interval. For example, for the Plant field in Figure
18.1, you can enter only a selection interval. But what if you want to exclude a certain
plant within the plant range on the selection screen, or include two plants in addition
to those given in the plant interval? All of this and several other options are available
via the Multiple Selection option that’s available in all information systems and reports
of all components. Choose Multiple Selection in Figure 18.1 for Material. In the
resulting screen, four tabs allow you to include or exclude single values or even an
entire range (see Figure 18.2).
Figure 18.2 Multiple Selection

You can enter information in each of the four tabs, and the ensuing output (report) will
show the desired results. You’ll also find available icons to further facilitate the busi-
ness user, such as copying data from a clipboard, adding or deleting a line within the
values, or using the Multiple Selection option. The Multiple Selection icon enables the
user to select multiple values by selecting the requisite checkboxes.
18.1.3 Maintain Selection
A frequently used and available option is Define Selection Options. When you choose
Define Selection Options (the leaf icon; see Figure 18.2), the Define Selection Options
screen appears. To take a shortcut to this screen, double-click the relevant field of the
selection screen of any report (see Figure 18.3).
Figure 18.3 Define Selection Options
18.1.4 Maintain Variant
Maintaining a variant in SAP is similar to saving a layout, which is then available for
repeated use when needed. You can also set a variant as default by managing your lay-
out options. For example, say that when you use the report for quality scores history,
you always use plant 1000 and the date range of 30 days from today. Instead of enter-
ing these parameters every time you run the report, you can save these details as a vari-
ant, which you can then subsequently select.
There are two areas where you can maintain variants. The first one is on the Initial
Parameters Selection screen of any report, information system, or analysis when defin-
ing the selection parameters. Simply enter the information once in the parameters
© 

775
18.1 The Basics of Reporting
selection screen, and proceed to save the variant by choosing More  Goto  Variants 
Save as Variant. On the Variant Attributes screen that appears, give the variant a name
and a short description, and then choose whether to make each field required, hidden,
or protected from data entry. With the variant saved, the next time you need to choose
More  Goto  Variants  Get the Variant. You can also delete incorrect or unwanted vari-
ants.
The second option to save a variant is when you’ve already executed an analysis or a
report. The system displays all listed fields, and you’ve made your required changes—
for example, applying any filter set, any sort of a column in ascending or descending
order, or any aggregation. You can then choose More  Select Layout, and then select the
Save Layout option from the dropdown. In the ensuing popup, enter the name of the
layout and a short description. Here, again, you can change or delete the saved layouts
if needed.
18.1.5 Inspection Lot Selection Worklist
When you execute the report by pressing (F8) or choosing Execute, a report such as the
one shown in Figure 18.4 appears, which is for the Inspection Lot Selection Worklist. In
this report, you’ll explore a few important options that are available, such as aggrega-
tion, setting a filter, or viewing the information in a graphical presentation. However,
some of the common and obvious options, such as sorting in ascending or descending
order of information and changing or displaying objects, aren’t covered.

18.1.7 Download
When you execute a report or conduct a standard analysis, you can also download the
information in one of the several available forms by right-clicking any column, fol-
lowed by choosing Spreadsheet. You can also send the information as an email attach-
ment or even perform an ABC analysis in the information system, although this option
is also available in the standard analysis reports.
18.1.8 Copy Selective Data to Microsoft Excel
You can copy selected data if you don’t want to download the full data of your SAP S/4HANA
system into Microsoft Excel or a different format. Press (Ctrl)+(Y) to select fields or con-
tent within the report. This enables block selection, in which you select the block of fields
you want to copy. Then, press (Ctrl)+(C) to copy the data. In Microsoft Excel or another
program (e.g., Notepad or Microsoft Word), press (Ctrl)+(P) to paste the copied data.
18.1.9 Print
To access the print option, choose the Print Preview icon within a report. It’s important
to note that all parameters used in the generation of the report in the information sys-
tem also become part of the printout, including filters and the like.

18 Reporting in SAP S/4HANA
780
18.1.10 ABC Analysis
As already mentioned earlier, you can also perform an ABC analysis in the quality
inspection worklist. Access Figure 18.10 by first clicking the Inspection Lot Quantity col-
umn, followed by clicking the ABC Analysis icon, located in the top menu bar shown in
Figure 18.4.
Figure 18.10 shows the A, B, and C divisions of inspection lot quantities based on the
user-defined division criteria of 70%, 20%, and 10%, respectively.
As discussed in the beginning of this chapter, while standard reports and SAP Fiori apps
provide real-time information, the standard analyses are more statistical in nature. The
ABC analysis we just discussed is based on real-time reporting; Section 18.2.5 will dis-
cuss the ABC analysis from a statistical perspective.
Figure 18.10 ABC Analysis
18.2 Standard Analyses
The standard analyses enable users to draw information from the available standard
information (info) structures in the SAP S/4HANA system. The difference between
reports such as Inspection Lot Selection and standard analyses is that in information
systems, the information is dynamic and changes when the business user performs the
relevant business functions. In standard analyses, the system draws from historical
information to enable the business user to make better business decisions. In other
words, data and information from information systems flow into analyses.
© 

781
18.2 Standard Analyses
Note
You can access standard analyses for all of the logistics areas of the SAP S/4HANA sys-
tem from the central location in the Logistics Controlling node of the SAP menu via
Logistics  Logistics Controlling.
You can then navigate to the relevant area’s standard analyses option. The SAP S/
4HANA areas for which the standard analyses are available are logistics, QM, inventory
controlling, purchasing, sales, shop floor control, shipment, and plant maintenance
(PM).
In the following sections, we’ll cover some of the standard analyses of QM. We’ll also
show a few features and functionalities available only in analyses and not in informa-
tion systems, such as time-series analysis and ABC analysis.

ling  QM Information System  Standard Analyses. Table 18.1 lists the transaction codes

division, there are further logical subdivisions for each analysis type, such as analysis

18.2 Standard Analyses
Figure 18.17 ABC Analysis
Figure 18.18 ABC Analysis for Values under Tolerance
The options in ABC analysis are as follows:
 Total ValueOverTol (%)
The total value of all the characteristics under or over tolerance are divided up by the
defined percentage.
 Number Suppliers (%)
The number of suppliers is divided up by the defined percentage.
 Valueover Tol (Absolute)
The actual number of characteristics with values under or over the defined tolerance
is divided up into A, B, or C segments.
 Number Inspection Characteristic
The number of master inspection characteristics is divided up into A, B, or C seg-
ments.

ABC analysis enables you to select the right strategy and then divides the key figures
into the top three groupings. You also have the flexibility to define the percentage of a
key figure to be listed in the A, B, or C segments.
In Figure 18.18, you have the flexibility to overwrite the system-suggested segment
sizes of A, B, or C. For this example, enter “40” for A Segment, “50” for B Segment, and
“10” for C Segment (not shown). These three entries mean that the system will divide
and display the Total ValueOverTol (%) in such a way that the top 40% will be catego-
rized in segment A, the next 50% in segment B, and the bottom 10% in segment C, in
sequential order. Choose Calculate (not shown) to open SAP Business Graphics, as
shown in Figure 18.19.
Figure 18.19 Graphical Representation: ABC Analysis

18.3 QM Cockpit for Evaluations
The QM Cockpit for Evaluations enables the business user to have access to all the
important information and data without using different information systems or navi-
gating to different reports or analyses. The QM Cockpit for Evaluations provides the
required information not only in tabular form but also in graphical form. It also
enables the business user to divide up the cockpit into various sections to have greater
visibility of information for comparison and analysis purposes.
To access the QM Cockpit for Evaluations, use Transaction QGA4 or follow menu path
Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Control  Evaluation of Original Documents 
General QM Evaluations (see Figure 18.21). This screen appears blank until you make the
necessary selections, for which you need to follow these steps:
1. From the dropdown menu, choose whether you want to evaluate inspection lots,
components, or notifications.
2. Choose Selection  Additional Selection (or press (F7)), and the system opens a
popup for you to choose whether you want inspection lots with defects or without
them. You can also choose to view archived data. Choose 01 Insp. Lot Selection w/o
Defects (Online).
3. In the Inspection Lot Selection screen, you can define the selection parameters, such
as plant 1100 and inspection type 01. You also have to define the grouping layout,
which is Standard, as well as the number of views (sections) that you want to see
appear in the QM Cockpit for Evaluations. For example, if you select 3 in Views (not
shown), then the system divides up the right side of the QM Cockpit for Evaluations
into three sections. For this example, choose a single view, and in the Grouping Lay-
out field (not shown), enter “1STANDARD”, which is the standard layout available.

In the following sections, we’ll cover some of the SAP Fiori apps of QM, such as Inspec-

18.4.1 Inspection Lot Analytics
The Inspection Lot Analytics app provides insights into several important key perfor-

made in the past year (365 days). The analysis can be based on time, inspection type,
material, or plant. You can view the KPIs in different ways by choosing from the follow-
ing options:
 Rejection Rate by Time Series
 Rejection Rate by Inspection Type
 Rejection Rate by Material and Plant
 Accepted and Rejected Lots by Time Series
 Accepted and Rejected Lots by Inspection Type
 Accepted and Rejected Lots by Material and Plant
 Lots Skipped and Not Skipped by Time Series
 Lots Skipped and Not Skipped by Inspection Type
 Lots Skipped and Not Skipped by Material and Plant
 Skip Rate by Time Series
 Skip Rate by Inspection Type
 Skip Rate by Material and Plant
Figure 18.25 shows the Inspection Lot Analytics app. The dropdown on the left side
enables you to choose a specific KPI to analyze in a specific way (see preceding list).
Here, along with graphical display, you can also view data a columnar form that is asso-

18.4.3 Record Inspection Results
Figure 18.30 shows the Record Inspection Results app. With this app, it’s possible to
record the results of characteristics flexibly and effectively. For example, you can
choose multiple inspection lots at one time and record the results centrally. On record-
ing results for the inspection lots, the app automatically valuates characteristics
according to valuation modes. Valuation modes define the rules for accepting or reject-
ing a characteristic and are discussed in detail in Chapter 3.

18 Reporting in SAP S/4HANA
796
Figure 18.30 Record Inspection Results
The Record Inspection Results app offers the following valuation modes:
 Valuation mode 100
When a sampling procedure uses this valuation mode, the valuation occurs when an
inspection plan consists of a sample size and acceptance number. The acceptance
number and the number of nonconforming units are compared.
 Valuation mode 400
When a sampling procedure uses this valuation mode, the valuation occurs when a
code (selected set) is assigned to a characteristic in an inspection plan.
 Valuation mode 500
When a sampling procedure uses this valuation mode, users can manually valuate
the characteristics in the inspection plan. This valuation mode also applies to char-
acteristics in inspection plans that are without sampling procedures.
 Valuation mode 700
When a sampling procedure uses this valuation mode, the valuation occurs when
the tolerance range is specified for characteristics in an inspection plan.
This app also shows long-term and open characteristics from different dimensions:
inspection lot, operation, sample, and master inspection characteristic. Long-term
characteristic refers to a criterion for which you can also record results after comple-
tion of the short-term inspection.
Figure 18.31 shows the options to apply additional filters that aren’t displayed on the
main screen of an app. To apply additional filters, choose Adapt Filters in Figure 18.30,
and the screen in Figure 18.31 appears. The option to use additional filters is available in
almost all SAP Fiori apps.

18.4.4 Results History
Figure 18.32 shows the Results History app. With this app, it’s possible to display the
results history for an inspection plan characteristic or a master inspection characteris-
tic. The valuation of a characteristic is shown as a graphic for the selected inspection
lots to compare inspection results over a longer period of time. The following are some
of the other features available in this app:
 Only displaying the results history for quantitative characteristics is possible.
 In the list, you can use the Settings to specify the grouping characteristics according
to which the inspection lot results are summarized. The grouping characteristics are
indicated by the suffix (Characteristic) or (Char).
 The individually selected inspection lot results are summarized as one aggregated
object according to whether they match the grouping characteristics. If, for example,

18.4.19 Characteristic Detailed Analytics
Figure 18.54 shows the Characteristic Detailed Analytics app that you can use to analyze
inspection characteristics for which results have already been recorded. The analysis
can be based on various categories, such as accepted and rejected inspections, rejection
rate, skip rate, mean value, standard deviation, cp and cpk indices, and so on, based on
time, inspection characteristics, master inspection characteristics, work center, plant,
material, supplier, and customer. The dropdown offers other associated characteristics
analytics, such as mean values and under-tolerance and over-tolerance values of mas-
ter inspection characteristics.
The values of cp and cpk are the process capability indices. The first value (cp) is a mea-
sure for the process dispersion (is the process controlled?)—that is, how closely a pro-
cess is running to its specification limits relative to the natural variability of the
process. The second value (cpk) describes the position of the mean value in relation to
the tolerance limits and therefore indicates whether the process is capable. The cpk is
an adjustment to the cp, affecting its noncentered distribution. In other words, cpk
measures how closely the target values are consistent with normal performance. For a
controlled and capable process, both values should be higher than 1.33. In many indus-
tries, the minimum requirement for a process capability index is now 2.0 or higher!

Figure 18.58 Manage Batches
If you create a new batch or edit an existing batch, all changes are saved as a draft ver-
sion as long as you don’t select Save. For 20 minutes, the draft version is available.
During this period, users with authorization can resume or discard this draft version. If
you want to reopen a draft version after more than 20 minutes, the system forces you
to discard the draft version. This is because the draft version locks all data used in the
batch entry for all users—for example, material data. To limit the time all data is locked,
the draft version can only be resumed for 20 minutes. Draft versions of a batch can be
found using selection criteria and filters. If you open a draft version, the system dis-
plays a warning, asking if you want to resume or discard the draft version. With this
app, it’s possible to trigger follow-up activities such as the following:
 Transfer stock of one batch of a material to another within a plant.
 Get a stock overview of a single material within a plant and a storage location.
 Perform further analysis and control options such as calling up the batch master for
changing and displaying master data, classification data, and the batch where-used
list containing information about the lifecycle of a batch.
